assistant_message:
I would not redesign the full-service offer. I would increase first-30-day gross profit by moving the existing pre-designed room packages into an immediate, prescribed upsell after the diagnostic or core-service sale. The Money Models goal is to sequence offers so CAC is minimized and gross profit collected in the first 30 days is maximized [money-models-offer-stacks:0]. Payback improves when gross profit exceeds CAC sooner, and the source specifically points to better or new offers in the first 30 days, timed at the moment the next problem exists [payback-period:0] [payback-period:2].

For this business, the cleanest move is: keep the $15,000 full-service design offer intact, then offer a $5,000 room-package add-on only after the client has seen the listing/photo audit and the gap is obvious. Frame it as the fastest path to fix the highest-ROI rooms before launch, not as more design scope. Use a short menu: primary bedroom, living room, outdoor/patio, and photo-ready accessory bundle. Prescribe one or two packages based on the audit, then ask which priority room they want installed first.

This should raise early gross profit without changing the core promise because it monetizes an adjacent need during the client's active buying window. With roughly $10,000 first-30-day gross profit against about $1,000 CAC already, the point is not survival; it is to turn a strong first-sale model into a stronger self-funded acquisition model.
